name: operations-support-maps-dispatch
executionConcern: DSH operational workboards, dispatch/custody, support/incidents/rescue, cart diagnostics, maps/service-area/privacy and direct affected readbacks
objective: Close operator intervention at DSH/Providers owners with legal transitions, isolation, idempotency/concurrency, privacy and canonical multi-surface readback.
truthOwner: DSH owns operational order/dispatch/support/rescue/service-area/address/privacy state; Providers owns external map-provider capability; WLT remains financial owner and is reference/read-only from these flows unless its own API is invoked.

tasks.objective: Close order, dispatch and custody interventions
tasks.currentProblem: UI-local eligibility, stale assignment/custody state or non-atomic retry can create duplicate or contradictory operational effects.
tasks.requiredChange: Trace operations/dispatch/handoff/rescue controls to DSH contracts/backend/database; enforce eligibility, expected state/version, atomic uniqueness, idempotency and audit/readback.
tasks.targetState: One legal DSH effect exists per operator intent and Captain/Client projections converge without exposing internal eligibility data.
tasks.action: Repair state-machine/database invariants at DSH, migrate adapters and remove UI-local final decisions.
mustNotChange: Do not calculate final eligibility only in UI.
Do not create two active assignments/rescue effects for one order.
Do not mutate WLT balance/commission inside DSH.
acceptanceCriteria: Concurrent/retried transitions cannot duplicate operational effect.
Captain/Client direct readbacks converge on committed DSH state.
tasks.rollback: Use legal DSH transition/forward repair for persisted operational state; never direct-edit around audit/state-machine constraints.
tasks.commitBoundary: One focused DSH operations/dispatch commit with database/contract changes only when root cause requires them.

tasks.objective: Close Support, incidents and order rescue
tasks.currentProblem: Disconnected ticket/incident/rescue state can leak cross-actor data, lose audit, accept stale transitions or show local success before commit.
tasks.requiredChange: Unify support/incident/rescue flows on DSH owner state machines with actor/object scope, expected-state conflict, idempotency, append-only audit and canonical readback.
tasks.targetState: Every support/rescue mutation has one durable scoped DSH effect; internal notes remain restricted and response loss is recovered by readback.
tasks.action: Trace Control Panel and direct Client/Partner/Captain support surfaces to shared/backend persistence and remove local-only state.
mustNotChange: Do not expose internal notes across actor scopes.
Do not reopen/transition outside legal state machine.
Do not make DSH rescue a financial writer.
acceptanceCriteria: Duplicate active rescue and stale transitions are prevented.
Audit/readback and response-loss recovery are deterministic.
tasks.rollback: Roll forward through DSH governed state when persistence changed; preserve audit evidence.

tasks.objective: Close maps, service-area, provider-health and privacy operator flows
tasks.currentProblem: Map/provider UI can confuse provider capability with service-area/address truth or expose sensitive address/audit data.
tasks.requiredChange: Keep provider capability in Providers and service-area/address/privacy in DSH; enforce topology/geofence/version/idempotency/privacy invariants and explicit health states.
tasks.targetState: Operator map/service-area/privacy state is owner-correct, scope-safe, privacy-safe and never based on production mock/fallback truth.
tasks.action: Trace Control Panel map sections through Providers and DSH map/service-area/address/privacy owners; correct binding and database invariants.
mustNotChange: Do not expose raw address PII in audit.
Do not accept client-selected service area without geofence resolution.
Do not treat provider configured state as operational health.
acceptanceCriteria: Invalid polygon/geofence/privacy transitions fail in owner/database layers.
Provider health and DSH service-area truth remain distinct and explicit.
Privacy audit structurally excludes prohibited PII.
tasks.rollback: Use forward migration/owner rollback compatible with retained privacy/audit evidence; never restore PII exposure.
